mainTopic: The miracles of the בית המקדש, the fire and smoke of the מערכה, and the end of פרק שבעת ימים
overview: This amud finishes the discussion of the miracles in the בית המקדש. First, the גמרא explains that the שולחן could become impure because it was lifted to show the עולי רגלים that the לחם הפנים stayed warm all week. Next, it asks why the golden trees of שלמה are missing from the list of miracles. It answers that permanent miracles are not counted, which also explains why the ארון and כרובים are missing. The גמרא then asks how the list can mention smoke from the מערכה when a ברייתא says the fire made no smoke. It answers that the smoke came from the fire the כהנים brought, not from the heavenly fire. It also explains that the heavenly fire looked like a lion in the מקדש ראשון and like a dog in the מקדש שני, where it was present but did not help burn. A ברייתא then lists six kinds of fire. Finally, the גמרא explains that wind made the smoke sway without scattering it, and it resolves a contradiction about east and west winds before the הדרן closes פרק שבעת ימים.

steps.title: Why would the table ever need to be declared pure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that the שולחן needed special purity protection. A wooden vessel made to stay in one place cannot become impure in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a wooden vessel made to stay in one place. Any wooden vessel made to stay in one place cannot become impure, and it even blocks impurity from spreading.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is attacking the earlier statement that the שולחן was 'pure'. Its point is that the שולחן could never have become impure to begin with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a wooden כלי that is never moved, a כלי העשוי לנחת, is not מקבל טומאה at all. It even acts as a barrier against impurity, like a wall. So saying the שולחן is 'טהור' seems pointless, because it was never at risk.

keyTerms.meaning: A wooden vessel
Made to rest in a fixed place, not moved around
Able to become ritually impure
Blocks impurity from passing through

phrases.english: It is a wooden vessel made to rest in place,
phrases.notes: Said about the שולחן, the table of the לחם הפנים

phrases.english: and any wooden vessel made to rest in place
cannot become impure,
and it blocks impurity from spreading.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question 'why?' on the previous amud, about the purity of the שולחן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement that the שולחן was pure, or needed to be kept pure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A כלי עץ העשוי לנחת cannot receive טומאה, so there is nothing to protect.

steps.title: The table was lifted to show the pilgrims the warm bread
steps.stepSummary: The שולחן was lifted up to show the עולי רגלים the miracle of the לחם הפנים. Because it was moved, it was no longer a 'resting' vessel, so it could become impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this teaches that they would lift it up to show the festival pilgrims, and tell them: See how beloved you are before ה׳! The bread is as warm when it is removed as when it was set out, as the verse says: 'to put out hot bread on the day it was taken away.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The שולחן was actually moved, because the כהנים lifted it to show the pilgrims the miracle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the שולחן was lifted sometimes, it was not truly a 'resting' vessel. That means it could become impure, so it did need to be kept טהור. The answer also shows that the miracle of the לחם הפנים was public: the bread stayed warm for a whole week.

keyTerms.meaning: Pilgrims who came up to ירושלים for the festivals
How beloved you are before ה׳
Its removal is like its arrangement, meaning the bread is just as fresh and warm
Warm bread

steps.whyThisMatters: A vessel's status as 'resting' depends on how it is actually used. Even occasional lifting makes the שולחן able to become impure.

phrases.english: Rather, it teaches that they lift it up
for the festival pilgrims,
and they say to them:
See how beloved you are before ה׳,
for its removal is like its arrangement,
phrases.notes: The bread was still warm a week later

phrases.english: as it says: 'To put out hot bread'
on the day it was taken away.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the שולחן was in fact moved
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The שולחן always stayed in place, so it could never become impure.
steps.terutzMaskana: The שולחן was lifted to show the pilgrims, so it was not a 'resting' vessel and could become impure.

steps.title: What about the golden trees of שלמה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the list of miracles leaves out the golden trees that שלמה planted, which grew real fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there no more miracles? But רב אושעיא said: When שלמה built the מקדש, he planted all kinds of golden fruit trees in it. They gave fruit in their season, and when the wind blew, the fruit fell, as it says: 'His fruit will rustle like Lebanon.' When the non-Jews entered the היכל, the trees dried up, as it says: 'The blossom of Lebanon withers.' And in the future, הקדוש ברוך הוא will bring them back, as it says: 'It will blossom abundantly and rejoice, with joy and song; the glory of Lebanon will be given to it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the count of miracles in the מקדש. It brings another miracle, the golden fruit trees, that is not on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה quoted earlier (עשרה ניסים נעשו לאבותינו בבית המקדש) gave a set number of miracles: ten. רב אושעיא describes golden trees that grew fruit, dried up when the non-Jews entered the היכל, and will come back in the future. If this miracle is real, why was it not counted?

keyTerms.meaning: And is there nothing more?
Precious fruit trees made of gold
The Sanctuary building of the מקדש
'Lebanon', a name the חז״ל used for the מקדש

steps.confusionAlert: 'לבנון' in these verses is not the country. חז״ל read it as a name for the בית המקדש.

phrases.english: And is there nothing more?
But didn't Rav Oshaya say:
When Shlomo built the Holy Temple,

phrases.aramaic: נָטַע בּוֹ כׇּל מִינֵי מְגָדִים שֶׁל זָהָב,
phrases.english: he planted in it all kinds of golden fruit trees,
and they produced their fruit in its season,
and when the wind blew on them, the fruit fell,
as it says: 'His fruit will rustle like Lebanon.'
And when the non-Jews entered the Sanctuary, it dried up,
as it says: 'And the blossom of Lebanon withers,'
and the Holy One, Blessed be He, will bring them back in the future,
as it says: 'It will blossom abundantly and rejoice,'
'even with joy and singing,'
'the glory of Lebanon will be given to it.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the שולחן, the גמרא challenges how complete the list of miracles is.
steps.kashyaTarget: The fixed count of ten miracles in the מקדש listed in the משנה (אבות ה:ה)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב אושעיא describes another miracle, the golden fruit trees, that is missing from the list.

steps.title: Permanent miracles are not counted
steps.stepSummary: The list only counts miracles that kept happening again and again. It does not count miracles that were a fixed, permanent feature.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא does not count permanent miracles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why the golden trees are not on the list. They were a permanent miracle, and the list does not include that kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה counts miracles that happened as repeated events in the service of the מקדש. A miracle built into the place itself, which was always there, belongs to a different group. So it is left off the list.

keyTerms.meaning: Permanent, fixed miracles
He does not count them

phrases.english: He does not count permanent miracles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list includes every miracle that happened in the מקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only includes miracles that kept happening as events, not permanent ones.

steps.title: This also explains why the ארון and כרובים are missing
steps.stepSummary: The new rule about permanent miracles also solves an earlier difficulty: why the ארון and כרובים were not on the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this answer: the ארון and the כרובים are also permanent miracles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies the answer it just gave to the earlier question about the ארון and כרובים. They are also permanent miracles, which explains a second way why they are not counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא explained that the ארון and כרובים were left off because only miracles seen outside are counted, not those inside the היכל. Now that it has the rule 'permanent miracles are not counted,' it gives a simpler reason: the ארון and כרובים were permanent miracles too. One rule now explains both omissions.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this answer
The Ark and the golden cherubs on top of it

steps.whatToRemember: The list of miracles in the מקדש counts only miracles that kept happening as events. Permanent miracles, like the golden trees and the ארון and כרובים, are not counted.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this:
the Ark and the cherubs too,
they are permanent miracles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 4 to resolve an earlier difficulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the new rule to an earlier question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ארון and כרובים were left off only because they were miracles inside the קודש הקדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are permanent miracles, so they are not counted.

steps.title: Quoting the smoke of the woodpile from the list
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the list of miracles and quotes one item: the smoke of the מערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: 'And the smoke of the woodpile.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting an item from the earlier list. This is a setup line for the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list said that even strong winds could not move the smoke rising from the מערכה. The גמרא quotes this line so that it can question it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The master said', a phrase used to quote an earlier source in order to discuss it
The arranged pile of wood burning on the מזבח

phrases.english: The master said: 'And the smoke of the woodpile.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section about a different item on the list of miracles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The list includes the miracle that the smoke of the מערכה was not moved by the wind.

steps.title: But the altar fire gave off no smoke!
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea of 'smoke of the woodpile' using a ברייתא. That ברייתא says the fire on the מערכה did not give off any smoke.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there really smoke from the woodpile? But a ברייתא teaches: Five things were said about the fire of the woodpile. It crouched like a lion, it was bright like the sun, it had real substance, it burned wet wood like dry wood, and it did not give off smoke!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the item it just quoted. A ברייתא says the fire on the מזבח made no smoke at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list of miracles speaks of smoke from the מערכה. But the ברייתא lists five special features of that fire, and the last one is that it gave off no smoke. The two sources seem to contradict each other, and the גמרא will need to resolve this.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
Crouching like a lion
It had real substance that could be felt
Wet wood just like dry wood

phrases.english: And was there smoke from the woodpile?
But it was taught: Five things were said
about the fire of the woodpile:
it crouched like a lion,
and it was bright like the sun,
and it had real substance,
and it burned wet wood like dry wood,
and it did not give off smoke!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the item quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The mention of 'smoke of the woodpile' in the list of miracles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says the fire of the מערכה gave off no smoke, so there was no smoke to be unaffected by the wind.

steps.title: The smoke came from the fire the כהנים brought
steps.stepSummary: The smoke in the miracle came from the ordinary fire people brought. The ברייתא that says 'no smoke' means only the fire from heaven. There is a מצוה to add human fire even though fire comes down from heaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: When we talk about smoke, we mean the fire brought by a regular person. As the ברייתא teaches: 'And the sons of אהרן the כהן shall put fire on the altar.' Even though fire comes down from heaven, it is a מצוה to bring fire made by people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 7. Two kinds of fire were on the מזבח. Only the heavenly fire had no smoke. The fire people brought did make smoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא about 'no smoke' and the miracle about smoke are talking about two different fires, so they do not clash. The proof that there were two fires is the פסוק 'ונתנו בני אהרן הכהן אש'. It teaches that the כהנים must bring their own fire even though heavenly fire is already there.

keyTerms.meaning: A regular person; here, fire made by people and not from heaven
As it was taught in a ברייתא (introduces a source)
Fire that comes down from heaven
It is a מצוה to bring

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the heavenly fire made smoke. It did not. The smoke miracle is only about the human fire that sat on the same מזבח.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea for the rest of this passage. The מזבח had both a heavenly fire and a human fire, and the two worked differently.

phrases.english: When we said (there was smoke), it was about the fire of a regular person.
As it was taught: 'And the sons of Aaron the priest shall put'
fire upon the altar,'

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵשׁ יוֹרֶדֶת מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: even though fire comes down from heaven,
it is a מצוה to bring fire made by a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by splitting the fire into two kinds
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: heavenly fire versus human fire
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There was only one fire on the מזבח, and it made no smoke, so a smoke miracle makes no sense
steps.terutzMaskana: Human fire was also on the מזבח, and it did make smoke; the miracle concerns that smoke

steps.title: Quoting the next miracle: the fire crouched like a lion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא of five features of the fire of the מערכה, quoted in step 7. It quotes the first feature: the heavenly fire crouched like a lion.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Crouching like a lion.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the first feature from the ברייתא in step 7: the heavenly fire looked like a lion lying down. This is a setup line, and the next step will challenge it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 quoted the miracle list. This step instead quotes the ברייתא of five features brought in step 7. It brings up a new detail about the heavenly fire, its shape, so the גמרא can examine it.

keyTerms.meaning: Crouching, lying down
Like a lion

phrases.english: (The fire was) crouching like a lion.
phrases.notes: A quote from the ברייתא of five features of the fire, cited in step 7

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of five features of the fire, cited in step 7, and examines its first item
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The heavenly fire on the מזבח looked like a crouching lion

steps.title: An eyewitness says the fire looked like a dog
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים saw the fire himself. He said it crouched like a dog, not a lion.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: רבי חנינא, the deputy כהן גדול, said, 'I saw it, and it was crouching like a dog!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the 'lion' description. It cites a ברייתא in which a כהן who saw the fire himself says it looked like a dog.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A lion is big and strong, and a dog is smaller and weaker. An eyewitness report seems to contradict the ברייתא of five features of the fire, so the two sources clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But was it not taught (introduces a challenge from a ברייתא)
The deputy to the כהן גדול
Like a dog

phrases.aramaic: וְהַתַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים:
phrases.english: But was it not taught: Rabbi Ḥanina, the deputy of the priests, said:
I saw it, and it was crouching like a dog!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַתַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the description quoted in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the fire crouched like a lion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An eyewitness ברייתא gives a different shape (a dog), which contradicts the lion description

steps.title: Lion in the first מקדש, dog in the second
steps.stepSummary: Both are true, at different times. The fire looked like a lion in the מקדש ראשון and like a dog in the מקדש שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here (the lion) is in the first מקדש. There (the dog) is in the second מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by saying each source speaks about a different מקדש. רבי חנינא lived during the second מקדש, so he saw the smaller 'dog' fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction is solved by time, not by rejecting either source. The heavenly fire was stronger in the מקדש ראשון and weaker in the מקדש שני.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult (introduces an answer)
The first בית המקדש (built by שלמה)
The second בית המקדש

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here — in the First Temple,
there — in the Second Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The lion and dog descriptions describe the same fire and contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: Lion means the first מקדש; dog means the second מקדש

steps.title: Was there heavenly fire in the second מקדש at all?
steps.stepSummary: The answer in step 11 assumed heavenly fire in the מקדש שני. רב שמואל בר אינייא says fire was one of five things the מקדש שני did not have.
steps.simpleTranslation: Was there (heavenly fire) in the second מקדש? But רב שמואל בר אינייא said: What does the פסוק mean, 'I will be pleased with it and I will be honored (ואכבד)', while we read it 'ואכבדה'? Why is the letter ה׳ missing? It stands for five things that were different between the first and second מקדש: the ארון, the כפורת, and the כרובים; fire; the שכינה; רוח הקודש; and the אורים ותומים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the answer it just gave. It quotes a teaching that the מקדש שני had no heavenly fire, so how could רבי חנינא have seen it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In חגי, the word is read ואכבדה but written without the final ה׳. Since ה׳ equals five, this hints at five things missing from the מקדש שני, and 'fire' is on the list. If there was no heavenly fire, step 11's answer seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Was there? (a doubting question)
But did he not say (introduces a contradicting statement)
We read it (the קרי, how the word is pronounced)
Missing the letter ה׳ (worth five)
The Divine Presence
The holy names in the כהן גדול's breastplate, used to get answers from ה׳

steps.confusionAlert: The list names more than five items, but ארון, כפורת, and כרובים count as one item. That makes exactly five, matching the ה׳.

phrases.english: And was there (heavenly fire) in the Second Temple?
But didn't Rav Shmuel bar Inya say:
What is that which is written: 'And I will be pleased with it and I will be honored (ve'ekkaved),'
phrases.notes: חגי א:ח, said about the second מקדש

phrases.english: and we read it 've'ikkavda' (with a heh).
Why is it missing the letter heh?
These are five things

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיוּ בֵּין מִקְדָּשׁ רִאשׁוֹן לְמִקְדָּשׁ שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: that were different between the First Temple and the Second Temple,
and these are they: the Ark, the Ark cover, and the cherubs,

phrases.aramaic: אֵשׁ, וּשְׁכִינָה, וְרוּחַ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ, וְאוּרִים וְתוּמִּים.
phrases.english: fire, and the Divine Presence, and the Divine Spirit, and the Urim VeTummim.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבְמִקְדָּשׁ שֵׁנִי מִי הֲוַאי? וְהָאָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אִינְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the assumption behind the answer in step 11
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that heavenly fire existed in the מקדש שני (looking like a dog)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב שמואל בר אינייא lists fire among the things missing in the מקדש שני, so רבי חנינא could not have seen heavenly fire there

steps.title: The fire was there, but it did not help burn
steps.stepSummary: Heavenly fire did exist in the מקדש שני. It just did not help consume the קרבנות, and that is the sense in which it was 'missing'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Yes, it was there. But it did not help (burn the קרבנות).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both statements are true. The heavenly fire could be seen in the מקדש שני, but it did not do the work of burning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Missing' in רב שמואל בר אינייא's list means missing in function, not missing completely. So רבי חנינא could really see the fire, which looked like a weaker 'dog', even though it did not burn the קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: They say (an unnamed answer)
It did exist
It did not help (burn)

steps.whatToRemember: The heavenly fire was like a lion in the first מקדש. In the second מקדש it was like a dog: it was there and could be seen, but it did not help burn the קרבנות.

phrases.english: They say: Yes, it did exist,
but it did not help (burn the offerings).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining 'missing' as lacking function rather than lacking existence
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Fire is listed as missing, so it was not there at all
steps.terutzMaskana: The fire was present and visible but did not help consume the קרבנות

steps.title: A ברייתא listing six kinds of fire
steps.stepSummary: Since the topic is the fire of the מזבח, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that lists six kinds of fire.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There are six kinds of fire. Some fire eats but does not drink. Some drinks but does not eat. Some eats and drinks. Some eats wet things just like dry things. Some fire pushes away other fire. Some fire eats other fire.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא connected to the topic of fire. It lists six kinds of fire, and the גמרא will explain each one next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Eats' means it burns solid things, and 'drinks' means it burns up liquids. The list moves from ordinary fire to special heavenly fires that are stronger, including fire that burns wet things or even other fire.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן taught (introduces a ברייתא)
Kinds of fire
Eats, meaning burns solid things
Drinks, meaning burns up liquids
Pushes away

phrases.english: The Sages taught: There are six kinds of fire:
there is fire that eats (solids) and does not drink (liquids),
and there is fire that drinks and does not eat,
and there is fire that eats and drinks,
and there is fire that eats wet things like dry things,
and there is fire that pushes away fire,
and there is fire that eats fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related source brought because the discussion is about the fire of the מזבח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are six kinds of fire, which differ in what they can burn

steps.title: Four fires: eating, drinking, both, and burning wet like dry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא identifies four of the six fires: ordinary fire, the fever of a sick person, the fire of אליהו, and the fire of the מערכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is fire that eats but does not drink. That is our ordinary fire. Fire that drinks but does not eat is the fever of sick people. Fire that eats and drinks is the fire of אליהו, as the פסוק says, 'and it licked up the water in the trench.' Fire that eats wet things as easily as dry things is the fire of the מערכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the list of six fires and explains which real fire each one is. These are the first four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'eating' means burning solid things and 'drinking' means drying up liquids. Ordinary fire burns wood but cannot dry up water. A fever dries out the body but does not burn the flesh. אליהו's fire did both, and the fire on the מזבח burned wet wood as easily as dry wood.

keyTerms.meaning: Eats, meaning it burns up solid things
Drinks, meaning it dries up liquids
Ours, meaning ordinary everyday fire
The trench אליהו dug around the מזבח and filled with water
The arranged pile of wood burning on the מזבח

phrases.english: There is fire that eats but does not drink
this is ours (ordinary fire).
Fire that drinks but does not eat
is that of sick people (fever).
Fire that eats and drinks
is that of Eliyahu, as it is written:
'And the water that was in the trench it licked up.'
Fire that eats wet things like dry things
is that of the wood pile on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first four items of the six fires introduced in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ordinary fire eats but does not drink. Fever drinks but does not eat. אליהו's fire did both. The fire of the מערכה burns wet wood like dry wood.

steps.title: Two more fires: fire that pushes away fire, and fire that eats fire
steps.stepSummary: The fire of גבריאל pushed away other fire. The fire of the שכינה consumed other fire, like when הקב״ה burned the angels.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is fire that pushes away fire. That is the fire of גבריאל. And there is fire that eats fire. That is the fire of the שכינה, as the master said: He stretched His finger among them and burned them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list with the last two fires. Each one has power over other fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גבריאל, an angel made of fire, pushed back the fire of the furnace to save חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה. The שכינה burned the angels, who are made of fire themselves. So the שכינה's fire consumes even fire.

keyTerms.meaning: Pushes away
The angel who saved חנניה, מישאל, and עזריה from the furnace
The Divine Presence
He stretched out His finger

steps.whatToRemember: There are six fires. Ordinary fire eats but does not drink. Fever drinks but does not eat. אליהו's fire eats and drinks. The מערכה's fire burns wet like dry. גבריאל's fire pushes away fire. The שכינה's fire eats fire.

phrases.english: There is fire that pushes away fire
that is the fire of Gavriel,
and there is fire that eats fire
that is the fire of the Shechina, as the master said:
He stretched His finger among them (the angels) and burned them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of six fires begun in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: גבריאל's fire pushes away fire, and the שכינה's fire consumes fire.

steps.title: People watched which way the smoke leaned, so the wind must move it
steps.stepSummary: An earlier teaching said no wind can move the smoke of the מערכה. But רבי יצחק בר אבדימי says that at the end of סוכות everyone watched which way the smoke leaned, to predict the year's rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it true that even all the winds in the world cannot move the smoke of the מערכה from its place? But רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said: At the end of the last day of סוכות, everyone watched the smoke of the מערכה. If it leaned north, the poor were happy and the homeowners were sad, because it meant plenty of rain and the stored produce would rot. If it leaned south, the poor were sad and the homeowners were happy, because it meant little rain and the produce would keep. If it leaned east, everyone was happy. If it leaned west, everyone was sad!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that wind never moves the מזבח's smoke. It quotes a teaching that describes the smoke leaning in different directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smoke can only lean north, south, east, or west if a wind pushes it. So רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's teaching seems to show that wind does move the smoke. That directly clashes with the claim that 'all the winds in the world' cannot move it.

keyTerms.meaning: The smoke of the wood pile on the מזבח
Move or shift
Watch closely
Homeowners, people with produce to store and sell
Rot

steps.confusionAlert: The poor are happy about heavy rain because there will be a big crop. Homeowners must then sell their produce quickly and cheaply before it rots, so the poor can buy cheap food. When there is little rain, it is the reverse.

phrases.english: And the smoke of the wood pile,
even all the winds in the world
do not move it from its place?
But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi say:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג
phrases.english: At the end of the last festival day of Sukkos
everyone watched the smoke of the wood pile.
If it leaned toward the north
the poor were happy and the homeowners were sad,
because the year's rains will be plentiful
and their produce will rot.
If it leaned toward the south
the poor were sad and the homeowners were happy,
because the year's rains will be scarce,
and their produce will keep.
If it leaned toward the east, everyone was happy.
Toward the west, everyone was sad!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the fire of the מערכה to its smoke, and questions an earlier teaching about that smoke.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier teaching that no wind in the world can move the smoke of the מערכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The smoke leaning in each direction is a sign of the coming year's rain. Leaning requires wind, so wind does move the smoke.

steps.title: The smoke swayed like a palm tree but never broke apart
steps.stepSummary: The wind made the smoke sway back and forth, but it never scattered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It went back and forth like a palm tree, but it never scattered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Wind did make the smoke lean, but it could not break up the column of smoke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle was never that the smoke stayed perfectly still. It was that the smoke stayed one solid column. Like a palm tree bending in the wind while its trunk stays in one piece, the smoke could lean in a direction without breaking up.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes and comes, meaning it sways back and forth
Palm trees
Scattered or broke apart

phrases.english: It goes back and forth like a palm tree,
but it never actually scattered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No wind could move the smoke at all, so it could never lean.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wind could make the smoke lean and sway, but it could never scatter it. That is what 'not moving it from its place' means.

steps.title: East and west winds: a clash with another teaching
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-quotes the lines about east and west. It then contrasts them with a ברייתא that calls the eastern wind always good and the western wind always bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: Toward the east, everyone is happy. Toward the west, everyone is sad. But a contradiction was raised: An eastern wind is always good, and a western wind is always bad. A northern wind is good for wheat when it has grown a third, and bad for olives when they are budding. A southern wind is bad for wheat when it has grown a third, and good for olives when they are budding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the end of רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's words and quotes them again. It then sets up a contradiction from a ברייתא about winds. Step 21 answers this contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the smoke leans east, a western wind must be pushing it. רבי יצחק בר אבדימי says that is a happy sign. But the ברייתא says a western wind is always bad and an eastern wind is always good, which seems to be the exact opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: And they set it against (another source), meaning a contradiction is raised
Eastern wind
Western wind
Reached a third of their full growth
Budding, the start of fruit forming

steps.confusionAlert: Smoke leaning east is caused by a wind blowing from the west. Keep track of which way the wind blows versus which way the smoke leans, or the contradiction will not make sense.

phrases.english: The master said:
Toward the east, everyone is happy;
toward the west, everyone is sad.
And a contradiction was raised:
An eastern wind is always good,
a western wind is always bad,
a northern wind is good for wheat
when it has reached a third of its growth,
and bad for olives when they are budding;
a southern wind is bad for wheat
when it has reached a third of its growth,
and good for olives when they are budding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: כְּלַפֵּי מִזְרָח הַכֹּל שְׂמֵחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the end of the teaching quoted in step 17 and raises a new contradiction about it.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's statement that smoke leaning east (a western wind) makes everyone happy, and smoke leaning west (an eastern wind) makes everyone sad.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says an eastern wind is always good and a western wind is always bad. That is the opposite of what the smoke signs suggest.

steps.title: A memory aid: the שלחן in the north, the מנורה in the south
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף (some say מר זוטרא) offers a memory aid for which wind helps which crop. The שלחן, which holds wheat bread, stood in the north. The מנורה, which burns olive oil, stood in the south. Each wind strengthens the crop that matches its side.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said, and some say it was מר זוטרא: Your memory aid is that the שלחן was in the north and the מנורה was in the south. This wind increases its own crop, and that wind increases its own crop!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the passage it started in step 19 by adding a memory aid for the north and south winds. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא answers the east-versus-west contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted passage taught that the north wind is good for wheat and the south wind is good for olives. To remember this, picture the היכל: the שלחן (wheat bread) stood on the north side, and the מנורה (olive oil) stood on the south side. Each wind 'increases its own,' meaning it helps the crop that belongs to its side. This step adds no new challenge, since the contradiction about east and west was already raised in step 19.

keyTerms.meaning: your memory aid (mnemonic)
and some say (introduces another possible speaker)
the Table in the היכל, which held the לחם הפנים made of wheat
the Menorah in the היכל, which burned olive oil
increases its own (helps the crop matching its side)

steps.confusionAlert: This memory aid is about the north and south winds only. The contradiction being solved is about the east and west winds. These are two separate parts of the quoted passage, so do not mix them together.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, וְאִיתֵּימָא מָר זוּטְרָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said, and some say it was Mar Zutra:
And your memory aid: the Table was in the north,
phrases.notes: The שלחן held bread made from wheat.

phrases.english: and the Menorah was in the south.
phrases.notes: The מנורה burned oil made from olives.

phrases.english: This one (the north wind) increases its own (wheat),
and this one (the south wind) increases its own (olives)!

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: קשיא (as the closing line of the re-quoted passage that leads into the contradiction)
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, וְאִיתֵּימָא מָר זוּטְרָא: וְסִימָנָיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the re-quoted passage from step 19 before the גמרא resolves the contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The north wind helps wheat and the south wind helps olives. You can remember this by the positions of the שלחן (north) and the מנורה (south).

steps.title: One source speaks of בבל, the other of ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the two sources do not argue. In בבל the east wind is good, but in ארץ ישראל the east wind is harmful.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this source is for us, and that source is for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from step 19 about the east and west winds. Each source is describing a different land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בבל has plenty of water, so a dry east wind does not hurt its crops and can even be good. ארץ ישראל has little water, so a dry east wind dries out the land and ruins the crops. Both sources are correct, each for its own place.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (the standard opening of an answer)
for us (in בבל)
for them (in ארץ ישראל)

steps.whatToRemember: The effect of a wind depends on the land. A dry east wind is fine in well-watered בבל but harmful in dry ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this source is for us (in Babylonia),
and that source is for them (in the Land of Israel).

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא — לַן, וְהָא — לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the east-versus-west contradiction raised in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different locations: each source applies to a different land.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two sources seem to directly disagree about whether the east wind is good or bad.
steps.terutzMaskana: The east wind is good in בבל, which has plenty of water, and harmful in ארץ ישראל, which has little water.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing the chapter שבעת ימים
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the first פרק of מסכת יומא, called שבעת ימים.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק שבעת ימים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא marks the end of the first chapter of מסכת יומא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional farewell said at the end of every פרק. It expresses the learner's hope to come back and learn the chapter again. The chapter is named after its opening words, which describe the seven days the כהן גדול is separated before יום כיפור.

keyTerms.meaning: we will return to you (the closing formula for a chapter)
Seven Days, the name of the first chapter of מסכת יומא

steps.whatToRemember: פרק שבעת ימים is now complete. It began with the כהן גדול's seven days of preparation and ended with a long section about the fire and smoke on the מזבח.

phrases.english: We will return to you,
Chapter Seven Days

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the winds discussion ends.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first chapter of מסכת יומא, שבעת ימים, is concluded.
